MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  NOVEMBER 12, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 4:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins; and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 4:31 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated Litigation

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins; and

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy,
  Environmental Sustainability Director; Maureen Tamuri, Interim Planning Director; Susan

  Deputy City Attorney; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Jason Lawrence, Deputy City
  Clerk; Kate Manisco, Recreation Manager; Tracey Rossine, Environmental Programs

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Norm Haynie led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 4:30 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  1  54956.9 and 54956.9(d)(l), with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council
  discussed the items on the Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action.

  REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  November l, 2024, with the amended agenda posted on November 8, 2024.

  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The motion carried unanimously.

  ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mitchell provided public comment.

  Interim City Attorney Rusin and City Clerk Pettij ohn clarified that public comment
  for items not the agenda would be heard after 6:30 p.m.

  Item Nos. l.B.5. was pulled by the Council.

  MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos. l.B.5. The motion carried
  unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
B.  New Items
  1.  Waive Further Reading
  Recommended Action: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive full
  reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/or second reading and adoption.
  2.  Approve Warrants
  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers
  73658-73860 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant
  Register No. 755 in the amount of the warrant appearing opposite their
  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $4,370,519.83. City of Malibu payroll check number 5485 and ACH
  deposits were issued in the amount of $785,197.34.
  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the September 11, 2024
  Special Meeting, the September l8, 2024 Special Meeting, the September
  23, 2024 Special Meeting, and the September 23, 2024 Regular Meeting.
  4.  Amendment to Agreement with Bureau Veritas North America, Inc. for
  Plan Check Consulting Services
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 1
  to Agreement with Bureau Veritas North America, Inc. to broaden the scope
  of work to include plan reviews of non-Woolsey proj ects.
  6.  Amendment to Agreement with Southwest Offset Printing
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 1
  with Southwest Offset Printing Co., Inc. for printing and mailing services
  of the Quarterly Recreation Guide and City Newsletter.
  7.  Third Amendment to Lease Agreement for 23661 Pacific Coast Highway
  (Super Care Drugs, Inc.)
  Recommended Action: Approve Third Amendment to Lease Agreement
  for 23661 Pacific Coast Highway with Super Care Drugs, Inc.
  8.  First Amendment to Lease Agreement for 23431 Pacific Coast Highway
  (Malibu Coast Animal Hospital)
  Recommended Action: Approve First Amendment to Lease Agreement for
  23431 Pacific Coast Highway with Malibu Coast Animal Hospital.
  9.  Amendments to Professional Services Agreement for School Separation
  Recommended Action: 1) Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No.
  9 to the Professional Services Agreement with STLR Corporation, dba
  Ryland School Business Consulting for a total contract amount of $587,710;
  and 2) Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 8 to the
  Professional Services Agreement with Kirk-Carter and Associates for a
  total contract amount of $224,430.
  10.  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the Existence of a Local
  Emergency Regarding Conditions on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH)
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24-57 extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency related to the increase of

  reckless and illegal driving on pacific coast highway and directing staff to
  coordinate efforts with other governmental agencies to increase attention
  and create programs to reduce the risk and danger associated with pacific
  coast highway in the City.
  ll.  Agreement with RTW Management, Inc.
  Recommended Action: Continue this item to the November 25, 2024
  Regular City Council meeting.
  12.  Professional Services Agreement Amendment No. 2 with Quinto
  Consulting, LP for City Treasurer Services and Request for Proposals
  Recommended Action: 1) Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No.
  2 to the Professional Services Agreement with Quinto Consulting, LP for
  City Treasurer services; 2) Direct the City Manager to develop and issue a
  request for proposals (RFP) for City Treasurer; and 3) Assign the
  Administration and Finance Subcommittee to review the proposals, conduct
  interviews, and make a recommendation to City Council regarding the
  selection of City Treasurer.

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  5.  Resolution Establishing an Irrevocable Election Period for Vacation and
  Sick Leave
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24-56 Amending personnel
  system rules Section 3 of Resolution No. 20—45 (Rule XIV. Vacation, Sick
  and Other Leave).

  Assistant City Manager Toney presented the staff report.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a
  motion to adopt Resolution No. 24-56 Amending personnel system rules
  Section 3 of Resolution No. 20-45 (Rule XIV. Vacation, Sick and Other
  Leave). The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation of Commendations to the Malibu Outreach Team

  Public Safety Coordinator Flores introduced the Malibu Outreach Team members.

  Mayor Stewart presented the commendations to the Malibu Outreach Team
  members.

  Zachary Coil, Program Director, thanked the Council for the recognition
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes ofNovember 12, 2024
  Page 5 of 11

  Presentation and Update on School Separation

  Deputy City Attorney Wood presented an update on school district separation and
  the City’s Los Angeles County Office of Education (LACOE) petition.

  The Council directed questions to Deputy City Attorney Wood.

ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  City Manager McClary stated the City was tracking election results and reported
  updates on the tallied votes. He announced the newly elected Councilmembers
  would be sworn in on December 9, 2024, and the meeting will be followed by a
  reception. He discussed the activation of the Emergency Operations Center (EOC)
  in response to the Broad Fire on Malibu Road and the hazardous wind conditions
  during the public safety power shutoff (PSPS). He stated the traffic signal
  generators were used where possible to keep signals working on Pacific Coast
  Highway (PCH) through the PSPS event. He discussed issues with cell service
  during the PSPS and the requirement for cell providers to provide generator backup.
  He discussed response to and damage from the Broad Fire. He stated the cause of
  the fire had not been determined. He stated staff meet with Supervisor Horvath to
  discuss PCH safety improvements. He stated the Califomia Department ofHousing
  and Community Development (HCD) was still reviewing the City’s draft Housing
  Element. He announced the extreme tides were proj ected for November and
  December. He stated he participated in the City Manager in Residence Program at
  Pepperdine University last Monday.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, City Manager McClary stated the City had
  an agreement with Caltrans allowing the City to provide generator power for signals
  on PCH during PSPS events. He clarified the cell providers were required to
  provide backup generators for their primary cell sites.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, City Manager McClary stated Caltrans was
  responsible for the signal lights. He stated the City’s agreement with Caltrans
  allowed the City to use its own generators to power the signals during emergencies.

  In response to Mayor Stewart, City Manager McClary confirmed that City Hall’s
  generator worked as expected.

RECESS  At 6:23 p.m., Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 6:30
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Mayor Stewart discussed the rules of decorum and the purpose ofpublic comment.

  Tim Pera, Mountains Recreation Conservation Authority (MRCA), presented the
  monthly ranger report. He stated there were continuous patrols for new
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes ofNovember 12, 2024
  Page 6 of 11

  encampments on MRCA property. He stated MRCA Rangers were working with
  the Malibu Outreach Team and Sheriffs Department on services for individuals
  experiencing homelessness. He stated 110 parking citations were issued last month.
  He discussed the Broad Fire that started on the Malibu Bluffs. He stated no
  encampments were present on the Malibu Bluffs prior to the fire. He stated five
  administrative citations were issued at Lechuza Beach for alcohol on the beach. He.
  stated all night ranger patrols were scheduled during the red flag event.

  ln response to Councilmember Silverstein, Ranger Pera confirmed the fire started
  on MRCA property and exact ignition point and origin was being investigated.

  Haylynn Conrad discussed the Woolsey Fire and questioned what Southern
  California Edison (SCE) had done to improve power safety and reliability. She
  recommended requesting information from SCE on power outages and investment
  in improvements in Malibu compared to other areas. She questioned why Malibu
  High School (MHS) does not have a generator. She discussed the challenges for
  residents when there is no power.

  Bill Sampson discussed his experience calling SCE during the PSPS event and how
  difficult it was to get information about when power would be restored. He
  discussed the importance of civility and the re-election of Councilmember
  Silverstein and Councilmember Uhring.

  Mitchell discussed legal action against the City from former staff member Adrian
  Femandez and individuals who will be named in the case.

  Paul Silvestre discussed Malibu Township Council (MTC) litigation over Trancas
  Park. He discussed Councilmember Uhring’s statement at a candidate forum that
  there was not lawsuit.

  Andy Lyon suggested requiring Zoom participants to provide their tilll name. He
  congratulated Councilmember Silverstein and Councilmember Uhring on their re-
  election.

ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Mayor Stewart stated he attended a Business Roundtable meeting and the Veterans
  Day event. He discussed the Broad Fire and the EOC activation. He discussed the
  extensive emergency experience of the City staff. He stated he had a readiness
  briefing with Mayor Pro Tem Riggins from City Manager McClary before the wind
  event. He discussed the protocols for PSPS events and the hazards created or
  exacerbated by PSPS events. He requested consensus to bring back an item to form
  an Ad Hoc Committee to address various PSPS hazards.

  Councilmember Silverstein indicated support for the item. He suggested
  considering forming an Ad Hoc Committee or Task Force. He suggested
  considering a declaration of local emergency in relation to PSPS events.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes ofNovember 12, 2024
  Page 7 of 11

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins indicated support for bringing back the item and
  considering directing the Public Safety Commission to address issues related to
  PSPS events.

  Councilmember Uhring indicated support for the item and discussed the urgency
  of addressing these issues.

  Councilmember Grisanti indicated support for the item. He discussed local grocery
  stores that had their own backup power and suggested looking for ways to support
  backup power for essential businesses.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins discussed using schools as evacuation sites and Starlink
  tools that could provide intemet service.

  Mayor Stewart stated Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) emergency
  sites had Wi-Fi capability.

  Councilmember Silverstein suggested bringing back an omnibus item to address all
  these options.

  In response to Mayor Stewart, City Manager McClary stated staff could bring back
  a report with options.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed the importance of undergrounding power lines
  in high-risk areas.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, Mayor Stewart stated SB 884 required
  circuits to be undergrounded, not service lines.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council: l) directed staff to bring back an item to: a) consider
  forming an Ad Hoc Committee, Task Force, or direct another advisory body to
  address issues related Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) events, and b) consider
  options for an emergency declaration as a result of PSPS events; and 2) directed the
  City Attomey to assign a legal advisor for these matters.

  Mayor Stewart requested City Manager McClary provide an update at the
  December 9, 2024 meeting.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed an individual who was stuck in the Surfrider
  Beach parking lot after the gate was locked. He stated the Veterans Day event had
  good participation. He stated the Seawolves swim team had sent him a copy of a
  proposal to share the pool with the Malibu Marlins. He thanked the Fire
  Department for its quick response to the Broad Fire. He requested an update on the
  fund balance reserve for emergencies. He indicated agreement with Mayor
  Stewart’s comments on the PSPS events. He discussed how PSPS events impacted
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes ofNovember 12, 2024
  Page 8 of 11

condo residents.

In response to Councilmember Uhring, Interim City Attorney Rusin explained the
purpose of the City Council policies and confirmed the City Council was the only
body that could change the policies.

Councilmember Uhring expressed concern City staff was not following the City
Council Policies. He discussed City Council Policy #43 and how complaints were
being reported. He discussed the code enforcement complaint against his property.
He requested a meeting with the City Attorney and City Manager. He thanked
those who voted for him in the November 5, 2024 election.

Councilmember Grisanti discussed the Halloween celebration in Malibu West. He
stated he attended a Business Roundtable meeting and the Veterans Day event. He
stated he attended the LACOE hearing in Santa Monica and encouraged the public
to attend the hearing tomorrow at MHS. He announced the new art exhibit
Feminine Perspectives at City Hall and the opening reception at City Hall on
November l7, 2024.

Councilmember Silverstein discussed the Broad Fire and the efficient Fire
Department response. He congratulated Councilmember Uhring and Haylynn
Conrad for their election to City Council. He commended Councilmember
Grisanti, Channing Frykman, and Andy Lyon for their campaign efforts. He
discussed PSPS events and potential mitigation measures that could be
implemented. He addressed Mitchell and stated his comments included inaccurate
information. He stated he attended the Veterans Day event and discussed the
importance of remaining non-partisan at such events. He asked if there was an
application for an Equinox Gym in The Park at Cross Creek and whether gyms
could be permitted in office buildings. He discussed staff statements at Planning
Commission meeting about the California Coastal Commission (CCC) and clarified
that staff did not speak directly with the CCC but spoke to CCC staff.

Mayor Stewart stated SCE had a list of generators and battery backups they would
pay a rebate for. He discussed the power sources for the circuits in the City.

In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Public Safety Director Duefias discussed
programs for medical backup batteries and backup batteries for seniors.
Mayor Pro Tem Riggins discussed generators and the noise impacts for the
neighborhoods. She discussed a small landslide on PCH near Latigo and Corral.

In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, City Manager McClary confirmed Caltrans
was notified of the slide last week and the K-rail stopped the debris.

Mayor Pro Tem Riggins announced a weed pulling event at Point Dume Headlands
on November 13, 2024 and the next Library Speaker Series event on November 20,
2024. She encouraged the public to attend the LACOE hearing at MHS. She
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes ofNovember 12, 2024
  Page 9 of 11

  encouraged everyone to shop local for the holidays. She stated she attended the
  Business Roundtable meeting, Veterans Day event, LACOE State of Education
  event. She stated she was online for the LACOE hearing on Friday and commended
  city staff and Councilmember Grisanti for their participation in the hearing. She
  congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember Uhring, and Haylynn
  Conrad on their election and thanked Councilmember Grisanti for his service. She
  discussed the April 23, 2009 lawsuit filed by MTC and subsequent settlement
  agreement that included a prohibition on sports league play at Trancas Canyon
  Park. She requested MTC and the City come to an agreement to remove that
  restriction.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Mayor Pro Tem Riggins requested
  consensus from the Council to bring back an item.

  Interim City Attorney Rusin advised on options get more information about the
  settlement agreement conditions.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed the City Manager to contact the Malibu
  Township Council regarding the restrictions on league play at Trancas Park and
  bring back more information

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins suggested Councilmember Uhring abstain from future
  discussions on this issue since he was a member of the MTC when the settlement
  agreement was entered into.

  Recommended Action: Continue this item to the November 25, 2024 Regular City
